items.title: Effects of Online Health Information Seeking Behavior on the Patient–Physician Relationship
items.abstract: With the widespread use of the Internet and digital technologies, online health information-seeking behavior has become an important factor associated with the patient–physician relationship. This review aimed to evaluate the relationship between online health information-seeking behavior and the patient–physician relationship in light of the current literature. English-language articles published between 2016 and 2026 were identified through a search of the PubMed database, and studies related to online health information-seeking behavior, the patient–physician relationship, health literacy, trust in physicians, and artificial intelligence were examined using a narrative review approach. The findings indicate that the relationship between online health information-seeking behavior and the patient–physician relationship is associated with the reliability of health information, health and eHealth literacy, trust in physicians, patient-centered communication, and individual characteristics. Reliable online health information has been associated with higher levels of patient engagement and shared decision-making, whereas inaccurate or misleading information has been associated with higher levels of health anxiety and problems related to trust and communication. Although artificial intelligence–supported applications may contribute to patient education, physician oversight is required for their safe use. Encouraging reliable sources of health information and supporting digital health literacy by healthcare professionals may contribute to strengthening a trust-based patient–physician relationship.

items.title: Efficient Safety Guardrails through Latent Dual-Hypothesis Reasoning with On-Demand Trace Reconstruction
items.abstract: Guardrail approaches that rely on reasoning-based large language models (LLM) improve safety decisions, but come with substantial inference overhead due to the explicit reasoning. We introduce LR-Guard (Latent Reasoning Guardrail), an efficient and explainable guardrail that jointly learns structured latent reasoning and on-demand reasoning reconstruction. Our method distills a frozen teacher's analysis of safe and unsafe prompt interpretations and their comparison into compact latent representations. Joint training optimizes these representations for both safety prediction and reconstruction of the teacher's explicit reasoning traces, enabling human-readable explanations without requiring intermediate text generation for every decision. Experiments show that LR-Guard outperforms its explicit-reasoning teacher in most in-domain and out-of-domain settings on safety classification and explanation extraction, while achieving a 19.4x inference speedup at batch size one. Further, reconstructed reasoning traces from the latent information exhibit high semantic similarity to the teacher's explicit reasoning.

items.title: Efficient training-free query routing framework for federated retrieval-augmented generation
items.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses in external documents retrieved at inference time. In federated RAG (FedRAG), documents are distributed across multiple autonomous corpora that cannot be centrally aggregated due to privacy, regulatory, or organizational constraints. A key challenge in FedRAG is query routing: selecting a subset of relevant corpora for each query without broadcasting to all participants. Existing routing approaches rely on supervised learning, requiring a uniform retrieval embedding model across corpora and costly retraining whenever the federation changes. These assumptions violate corpus autonomy and limit scalability in dynamic federated environments. We propose RAGSpot , a training-free query routing framework that enables efficient corpus selection without requiring a shared local retrieval embedding model. RAGSpot represents each corpus using compact cluster-level metadata derived from its vector index and estimates corpus relevance via query-to-cluster matching. In addition, it introduces a rank-based fusion strategy that jointly leverages document-level and corpus-level rankings to support robust aggregation across heterogeneous embedding models. Experiments with corpora from the BEIR benchmark show that RAGSpot improves retrieval accuracy over the strongest training-based router by 1.23– \(1.48\times\) in nDCG and 1.28– \(1.66\times\) in Recall, and over the strongest LLM-based router by 1.63– \(2.01\times\) in nDCG and 1.93– \(2.34\times\) in Recall, without any further training. Also, RAGSpot achieves query latency that is comparable to, or even lower than, that of SOTA methods on average.

items.title: Electric vehicle battery fault detection and diagnosis agent: Descriptive text modeling of battery digital signals
items.abstract: With the rapid proliferation of electric vehicles, the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries have become critical concerns. Effective anomaly detection is essential for ensuring safe battery operation. However, as battery systems and operating scenarios become increasingly complex, Battery fault diagnosis and maintenance increasingly require stronger adaptability to heterogeneous operating scenarios and intelligent human–AI collaboration. Traditional fault detection and diagnosis paradigms are usually tailored to specific scenarios and predefined workflows, making them less effective in complex real-world applications. To address the scarcity of open-source battery fault report corpora and the lack of unified maintenance knowledge representation, this study investigates a descriptive text modeling approach for battery signal reports. Monitoring signals, statistical features, anomaly records, and state assessment results are transformed into structured and readable natural language descriptions, thereby constructing a language corpus for battery health diagnosis and maintenance. Based on this framework, we propose VBFDD-Agent, a vehicle battery fault detection and diagnosis agent for automotive-grade battery systems. VBFDD-Agent integrates descriptive battery-state texts, historical case retrieval, local maintenance manuals, and large language model reasoning to generate structured diagnostic results and maintenance recommendations. Experimental results show that the proposed framework can accurately perform anomaly monitoring and provide flexible, efficient, and actionable maintenance suggestions. Expert evaluation further confirms the practical value of the generated recommendations.

items.title: Emerging Nephrology Nursing: Current & Future roles
items.abstract: Nephrology nursing has evolved significantly over the past decades, transitioning from task-oriented care to a comprehensive, patient-centered specialty that integrates clinical expertise, advanced technology, and chronic disease management.This review explores the emerging roles of nephrology nurses in the current healthcare landscape and envisions future directions shaped by technological advancements, healthcare reforms, and evolving patient needs.Current roles encompass not only hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis care but also kidney transplantation, conservative kidney management, patient education, and multidisciplinary collaboration.The increasing prevalence of chronic kidney disease and the complexity of renal replacement therapies demand advanced competencies, including leadership, research, and quality improvement.Future roles are anticipated to expand into telehealth, remote patient monitoring, artificial intelligence-assisted care, genomics-informed nursing, and community-based kidney health promotion.The integration of advanced practice nursing and nurseled clinics is expected to further strengthen chronic disease management and reduce hospital readmissions.This review highlights the need for continuous professional development, specialized training programs, and policy support to equip nephrology nurses for these evolving responsibilities.Emerging nephrology nursing roles are critical to addressing the global burden of kidney disease and enhancing the quality, accessibility, and sustainability of kidney care delivery.

items.title: Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in High-Performance Liquid Chromatographic Analysis: A Mini Review
items.abstract: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) is one of the most widely employed analytical techniques for the qualitative and quantitative determination of compounds. Despite its exceptional sensitivity and reliability, conventional HPLC method development and data interpretation often require extensive experimental optimization, expert knowledge, and considerable time. Furthermore, peak detection, integration, and identification in chromatograms can be automated by artificial intelligence (AI) methods like machine learning and deep learning, allowing for quicker and more precise analysis of complicated datasets, resulting in the identification of compounds and the comprehension of complex reactions more quickly and creatively. From an economic perspective, these developments promote sustainable analytical chemistry and effective resource recovery. Moreover, AI can increase productivity and reduce the possibility of human error by automating chromatographic analysis. Additionally, AI has played a key role in enhanced analysis of complicated spectra in fields like spectroscopy and chromatography, as well as in handling heterogeneous data. This mini review discusses recent advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning (ML) that enable scientists to address complex analytical challenges more effectively. It highlights the growing application of these technologies in chromatographic predictions, particularly in liquid chromatography method development. The present review further examines key AI-driven areas, including automated method development, retention time prediction, peak deconvolution, predictive maintenance, and intelligent data processing.

items.title: EmoGenie: Benchmarking and Evaluating Expressed and Evoked Emotion in T2I Generation with MLLMs
items.abstract: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) have significantly promoted using text-to-image (T2I) models to generate images with specific affective intentions. However, the emotional effects conveyed by generated images frequently deviate from target expectations, and it remains unclear whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can reliably interpret the emotion of AI-generated visual content. Existing affective benchmarks are predominantly built on natural images, while affective studies of generated images have largely focused on emotions expressed in portraits, lacking a unified benchmark for studying the emotions expressed and evoked by generated images. We therefore introduce EmoGenie, a benchmark of emotion for AI-generated images that evaluates capabilities in T2I generation and MLLM understanding across expressed and evoked emotions. It comprises 6,400 images generated by eight T2I models using 800 emotion-targeted prompts, annotated with question-answer (QA) pairs, termed EmoGenie-QA, and continuous human ratings, termed EmoGenie-Assess. EmoGenie-QA contains 90,000 closed-set questions in single-image and image-pair settings, as well as 1,057 open-ended questions for emotion description. EmoGenie-Assess benchmarks continuous affective and aesthetic prediction using 13,175 mean opinion scores (MOSs) aggregated from human ratings in terms of valence, arousal, dominance, and aesthetic quality. We further develop EmoProbe, which combines emotion question answering with response-aligned, dimension-specific regression heads for continuous score prediction. Experimental results show that EmoProbe achieves superior results on emotion-related QA tasks, while its affective and aesthetic predictions correlate better with human ratings, demonstrating its state-of-the-art capabilities of unified coarse-to-fine affective understanding for AI-generated images.

items.title: Empathetic responses by AI legal assistants and user over-disclosure: evidence from an online survey experiment
items.abstract: Introduction Generative AI legal assistants rely on users to describe events, evidence, and transaction histories, yet the same accounts may contain private information that is unnecessary for legal guidance. Empathetic language may affect how selectively users decide what to provide. Methods A one-factor between-subjects online survey experiment on Wenjuanxing randomly assigned 360 participants to rational, mildly empathetic, or highly empathetic AI legal responses (n = 120 per condition). Participants completed 1-5 Likert-type measures of parasocial response, privacy boundary judgment, and over-disclosure intention, together with related relational measures, and then answered an open-ended disclosure task. Results The empathy manipulation was successful, F (2,357) = 524.170, p < 0.001, and η 2 = 0.746. Stronger empathetic responses increased parasocial response (η 2 = 0.428), reduced privacy boundary judgment (η 2 = 0.242), and increased over-disclosure intention (η 2 = 0.406). The coded non-essential disclosure score rose from 0.994 in the rational condition to 6.132 in the highly empathetic condition, F (2,357) = 170.795, p < 0.001, and η 2 = 0.489. Necessary case facts remained stable, F (2,357) = 0.245, p = 0.783. Bootstrap analysis yielded an indirect effect through parasocial response of 0.214, 95% CI [0.151, 0.283], and a sequential indirect effect through parasocial response and privacy boundary judgment of 0.063, 95% CI [0.033, 0.098]. Discussion Within this consumer-dispute scenario, stronger empathetic cues reduced users' selectivity about which information was appropriate to provide. Data-minimization prompts and evidence-oriented questioning may help retain limited emotional support without encouraging unnecessary disclosure.

items.title: Encounter-Driven City-Scale Human Mobility Generation with Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for human mobility generation by modeling individual routines, activities, and mobility preferences. However, existing approaches remain largely resident-centric: generating realistic individual trajectories does not necessarily recover the encounters that emerge when multiple residents co-occur at the same place and time. To this end, we study encounter-aware human mobility generation, which jointly preserves individual mobility and population-level interaction structure. We propose EncounterMob, an encounter-driven LLM framework consisting of a coarse-to-fine Encounter Generator and an Iterative Coupling Framework. The Encounter Generator first captures city-level encounter rhythms and then instantiates participant-time-venue encounters, while the Iterative Coupling Framework coordinates these encounters with personal mobility behavior through successive refinement. We further introduce an encounter recovery protocol covering encounter marginal and joint distributions over residents, times, and venues. Experiments on the Japan and NYC datasets show that EncounterMob outperforms all external baselines on all seven encounter metrics and all six personal mobility metrics. Compared with ELLMob, it reduces the participant-time-venue joint error by 40.4%/41.7% and the mean personal mobility error by 58.8%/32.7% on Japan/NYC, respectively.

items.title: Enforcing a Strict Safety Margin in LLM Text Generation via Barrier Lyapunov Control
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed without formal guarantees against toxic text generation. Existing control barrier function (CBF) based safety filters can keep the generation trajectory within a toxicity-free region, but do not enforce a positive distance from its boundary, allowing formally safe trajectories to approach the toxicity threshold arbitrarily closely and leaving little buffer against modelling errors or disturbances. We address this limitation with a Barrier Lyapunov Function (BLF) safety filter that enforces a prescribed clearance margin throughout generation while retaining the continuous-time transformer dynamics, including feedforward layers. The resulting safe input set is a half-space defined by a constraint affine in the control input, and is non-empty under certified surjectivity and classifier-nondegeneracy conditions. For margin-compatible initial conditions we prove that the clearance margin is never violated and that the prescribed clearance is restored exponentially, yielding an explicit clearance floor, and show that, as the margin vanishes, the admissible trajectories satisfy the exponential second-order CBF condition. We further derive an explicitly computable sufficient disturbance budget under which the clearance guarantee degrades gracefully. Simulations on a small transformer illustrate the resulting improvement in safety clearance.

items.title: Engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells for hematological malignancies: genome editing, synthetic biology, and precision immunotherapy
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-based immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment by enabling engineered immune cells to selectively recognize and eliminate malignant targets, with CAR-T cells establishing the first major clinical success in this field. However, severe associated toxicities, logistical complexities of autologous manufacturing, and high rates of antigen-loss relapse have accelerated the development of alternative effector platforms such as CAR-NK cells. CAR-NK cells combine antigen-directed cytotoxicity with the innate antitumor functions of natural killer cells, offering a potentially safer and more readily available off-the-shelf therapeutic strategy. Nevertheless, the clinical efficacy of CAR-NK therapy is constrained by key biological and translational hurdles: brief in vivo persistence, inadequate trafficking and solid tumor infiltration, severe susceptibility to tumor microenvironment-mediated immunosuppression, and antigen escape driven by tumor heterogeneity. These biological constraints are compounded by technical bottlenecks, including cell source variability, limited large-scale expansion capacity, ex vivo functional exhaustion, and an absence of standardized manufacturing protocols. To address these multi-faceted barriers, recent advances in genome engineering, systems biology, and computational modeling provide promising routes forward. Given that prolonged exposure to immunosuppressive niches induces functional impairment, genome-editing strategies targeting inhibitory checkpoints and persistence programs are crucial; however, enhancing persistence requires stringent safeguards to mitigate toxicity risks from constitutive signaling or genomic instability. Thus, engineering next-generation CAR-NK cells necessitates balancing extended longevity, potent cytotoxicity, and safety. Multiomics approaches facilitate deeper characterization of CAR-NK functional states and tumor–immune interactions, whereas artificial intelligence–guided engineering integrates high-dimensional biological and manufacturing data to optimize receptor design, predict therapeutic performance, and accelerate translational workflows. Collectively, these innovations support a paradigm shift toward programmable CAR-NK cells that can dynamically sense, adapt, and respond to tumor evolution, driving the transition toward autonomous, highly scalable, and precisely controllable cellular immunotherapies in precision oncology.

items.title: Enhanced Detective: A Dual-Stage Proactive Defense Against Internal Poisoning Attacks in Financial Fraud Detection Using Federated Learning
items.abstract: With recent developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI), the adoption of distributed learning paradigms such as Federated Learning (FL) has emerged. In simple terms, FL enables multiple entities to collaboratively train AI models without sharing local data. The FL paradigm is particularly valuable in privacy-sensitive settings, such as financial services, because it enables institutions to collaboratively improve fraud-detection models while keeping sensitive transaction data local. However, FL schemes are prone to security vulnerabilities, where malicious clients can poison local data or model updates and degrade the global model, and hence the performance of the resulting model might be affected. Therefore, in this work, we propose Enhanced Detective, a dual-stage robust aggregation strategy that combines Median Absolute Deviation (MAD), distance-based update filtering, and FedMedian aggregation. Experiments on an imbalanced credit card dataset evaluate targeted label-flipping and weight-scaling attacks over 50 communication rounds. With 40% malicious clients, Enhanced Detective achieves an AUPRC of 0.796 and a Recall of 0.847.

items.title: Enhancing Prehospital Emergency Care Through Reliable Assessment of Consciousness Levels: A Structured Narrative Review
items.abstract: Altered level of consciousness (ALOC) is among the most frequent and most consequential presentations in prehospital emergency care. Registry data from unselected ambulance populations indicate that approximately one in eight transported patients has a reduced Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score, and that even mild reductions carry substantial 30-day mortality. Assessment of consciousness governs airway management, transport destination, and activation of stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI) pathways. The GCS and the AVPU scale (rendered AVDS in Portuguese-language services) are the instruments in routine field use, yet both were developed and validated predominantly outside the prehospital environment. This review addresses four questions: (i) the clinical importance of consciousness assessment in prehospital care; (ii) the reliability and validity of the GCS, AVPU/AVDS, and FOUR score, with specific attention to performance in EMS provider cohorts; (iii) the operational and human-factor determinants that degrade assessment accuracy in the field; and (iv) the current evidence for objective adjuncts to subjective scoring. We conducted a structured narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 2026, combining controlled-vocabulary and free-text terms across four concept blocks: consciousness; assessment instruments; prehospital/EMS setting; and reliability, validity, accuracy, and inter-rater agreement. Records were screened independently by two reviewers. Where a prior review was identified, its reference list was hand-searched and the underlying primary studies were retrieved and cited in preference to the review, so that evidence is not double-counted. Thirty-six sources form the synthesis corpus. A narrative rather than systematic design was chosen because the eligible literature is heterogeneous in design, population, and outcome metric to a degree that precludes meaningful pooling; the trade-offs of this choice are stated explicitly. Field GCS correlates with arrival GCS ( r = 0.67; n = 12,882) and the change between the two independently predicts mortality. The GCS is the most granular instrument, but its reliability is component-dependent, with the motor component consistently weakest; after structured training, weighted kappa reached 0.85–0.96 across components, motor response remaining lowest at 75.1% agreement. For AVPU/AVDS, large prehospital datasets localise disagreement precisely to the Verbal and Pain categories: in 4.3 million paediatric EMS encounters, overall AVPU-GCS accuracy was 0.95 (kappa = 0.61) but intraclass F1 fell to 0.37 for Verbal and 0.50 for Pain, against 0.98 for Alert; in 2,900 prehospital trauma activations, GCS differed significantly between all AVPU categories except Verbal versus Pain ( p = 0.18). The FOUR score shows modestly superior reliability and validity to the GCS in ICU and ED settings but has not been validated prehospitally. Substituting GCS-motor for total GCS increases undertriage in patients over 65 ( n = 4,480,185). Automated pupillometry substantially outperforms manual pupil examination (ICC 0.99 versus 0.92), and low Neurological Pupil Index (NPi) values are consistently associated with adverse TBI outcomes, though prognostic accuracy in isolation is moderate (AUC 0.66–0.68). Ambulance-based EEG recording is feasible but remains at proof-of-concept stage. The evidence supports specific, bounded recommendations rather than broad prescription. Calibration training should target the GCS motor component and the AVPU/AVDS Verbal-Pain boundary, which are the empirically identified loci of disagreement. Total GCS should be retained over GCS-motor for field triage, particularly in older patients, and all three components should be documented and handed over alongside the total. Automated pupillometry is the most mature adjunct and warrants piloting in defined high-yield scenarios. The central evidence gap remains the principal research priority: no study has directly compared GCS, AVPU/AVDS, and FOUR score reliability within a prehospital provider cohort under field conditions.

items.abstract: This thesis analyzes the didactic potential of using interactive and innovative pedagogical technologies to enhance students’ learning activity, cognitive engagement, educational motivation, and participation in collaborative activities within differentiated instruction. Particular attention is paid to adapting interactive methods to differences in students’ levels of knowledge, interests, pace of learning, and individual educational needs. The role of problem-based learning, project-based learning, gamification, cooperative learning, the flipped classroom model, multimedia tools, and other innovative approaches in differentiated instruction is examined.

items.title: Epeditor: A scalable platform for large-ensemble building energy simulation enabling agent-assisted automation
items.abstract: The data scale of energy simulation keeps increasing, particularly in urban building energy modeling (UBEM) and uncertainty analysis, where thousands of EnergyPlus runs are often required to explore complex parameter spaces and building variability. To simplify these data-intensive workflows, recent studies have introduced AI agents for end-to-end simulation tasks. However, in practice, both AI-assisted and conventional batch workflows remain constrained by unstable field inference and search bias, inefficient large-ensemble simulation execution, and cumbersome data processing. To address these problems, this study introduces Epeditor, a cloud-deployable simulation infrastructure for large-ensemble building energy analysis for both AI and human users. It combines three improvements on current workflows: a knowledge-assisted parameterization with more accurate and stable field search in IDF files; a simulator that improves parallel execution efficiency through Operating-System-Level deployment; and a data management system that enables memory-safe aggregation of large simulation inputs and outputs. The packaged Agent Skill allows AI agents to execute fully automated dataset generation, batch simulation, surrogate modeling, and interpretation through an auditable workflow. Epeditor is evaluated through a agent benchmarks with metrics for Artificial General Intelligence, and two case studies are introduced to show its ability in research and design practices including an AI-assisted surrogate-modeling case, and design-studio practices. The pipeline exhibits 99.98% robustness in IDF generation, up to four-fold acceleration in high-parallel simulation, and 76.28 ( F 1 ) in IDF field inference. These findings indicate that Epeditor can lower the technical and computational barriers to large-ensemble EnergyPlus simulation, supporting more accessible, reproducible, and AI-ready building energy analysis.

items.title: Epistemic Injustice in Generative AI: How Minority Language Systems Reproduce or Resist Digital Exclusion
items.abstract: Generative AI performance disparities can exclude minority-language speakers from digital participation. Drawing on Fricker’s epistemic-injustice framework, we examined five Chinese minority languages using four-way causal mediation decomposition, intersectional analysis, and participatory evaluation. Under the measured mediators and model specification, non-PIE components accounted for an average of 67.5% of observed disparities. Tibetan speech recognition yielded a 43.9% word error rate (WER) for elderly speakers using religious and dialectal language, 6.9 percentage points above the main-effects additive reference. Community evaluation prioritized religious sensitivity, while threshold rules identified culturally salient failures missed by linear weighting. CAML-LLM, integrating cultural knowledge graphs, multimodal alignment, and community-weighted training, reduced WER from 31.2% to 22.7% and improved cultural appropriateness by 22.5%. These findings characterize model-dependent disparities and demonstrate that participatory system design can improve minority-language performance within the evaluated settings.

items.title: Ethics and Use of Artificial Intelligence for Service Delivery in Nigerian Academic Libraries
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in library offers a transformative opportunity to enhance service delivery amidst persistent staffing and funding deficits. However, this technological shift creates tension regarding ethical governance, data privacy, and cultural representation. This study investigated the ethical dimensions and operational usage of AI for service delivery in Nigerian academic libraries, with policy frameworks, algorithmic justice, data privacy, and technological equity. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. The population comprised 8,323 certified librarians in Nigeria, from which a sample size of 368 was selected using a convenience/purposive sampling technique. Data collection was executed using a validated self-structured 5-point Likert scale questionnaire administered during the EDO 2025 Nigerian Library Association (NLA) Conference. A total of 318 valid copies were retrieved, yielding an 86.4% response rate. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including frequency counts, percentages, mean, and standard deviation. The results revealed that while librarians demonstrate a high overall level of ethical awareness and a desire for structural policy frameworks (M = 3.64), their specific practical awareness regarding daily data privacy and intellectual property implications remains high (M = 3.79). Result showed that current library professional ethics are moderate (M=3.36) to regulate AI adoption. Furthermore, respondents reported a moderately critical level of algorithmic bias moderate (M=3.10), strongly indicating that current Western-centric AI systems marginalize local research, regional cultural contexts, and indigenous Nigerian languages. Concerns surrounding data privacy, cloud breaches, and third-party commercial data-mining also scored moderate (M=3.18), exposing the vulnerabilities of libraries operating with sub-baseline digital infrastructures. The study concluded that forcing AI adoption without context-responsive ethical governance exacerbates algorithmic injustice and risks compromising user trust. It is recommended that stakeholders co-design localized AI deployment policies, conduct rigorous pre-deployment algorithmic audits, and establish human-AI collaborative frameworks for patron confidentiality against aggressive data mining.

items.title: Ethics, Bias, and Algorithmic Justice
items.abstract: Algorithms now shape who gets diagnosed, who gets treated, and who gets overlooked, and too often they reproduce the very inequities medicine claims to fight. This chapter examines how bias enters clinical artificial intelligence and what it costs patients. Drawing on systematic reviews and real cases, it traces the mechanisms, training data that underrepresents minority populations, models that learn from unequal patterns of care, and proxies like health spending that mistake access for need, producing tools that score black patients as healthier than they are. It looks at race correction in kidney and other algorithms, uneven accuracy across racial groups in cardiovascular and imaging models, and the transparency gaps that let these flaws go unnoticed. Finally, it turns to solutions, explainable AI that lets clinicians interrogate algorithmic logic, guiding principles for fairer design, and the regulation, accountability, and physician vigilance required to ensure these systems advance justice rather than entrench disparity.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Kazakh-Language Educational Assistants: Sentiment Classification and Question Answering with and Without Context
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in education, but evidence on their performance comes mainly from high-resource languages. We evaluated five commercial LLMs in Kazakh in a zero-shot setting: sentiment classification on 300 class-balanced KazSAnDRA reviews and question answering (QA) on the same 300 randomly sampled KazQAD questions with and without the gold supporting passage. Exact McNemar tests with Holm correction found no significant pairwise differences on sentiment classification, one with supporting context, and nine without context under the Containment criterion. For OpenAI and Anthropic, the higher-tier model had a larger advantage over its lower-tier counterpart when the supporting passage was removed (tier-by-regime interaction: OR = 1.92, 95% CI [1.52, 2.43]). Closed-book scores were affected by output format, inflectional morphology, and answer length. Human evaluation of 500 QA responses showed that string-based metrics substantially underestimated closed-book accuracy (0.55 by human judgement versus 0.26 by Containment). Under human judgement, the three higher-scoring models did not differ significantly from one another. Access to a relevant passage narrowed differences between models, although this oracle-context condition did not test a retrieval system. These findings support task-specific evaluation of Kazakh-language educational assistants and the use of answer-matching criteria checked against human judgement.

items.title: Executable Prefix Values for Locating Agent Failures
items.abstract: Work on debugging LLM agents treats the "first mistake" marked by a human or LLM judge as ground truth for where a trajectory failed. We ask whether such labels point at causes or symptoms, and make the distinction executable: we restart the agent from reconstructed intermediate states of a failed trajectory and estimate its prefix value V(h_t), the probability of success from each step, with a certified point of no return (PNR) for a failure. On 150 SWE-bench Verified tasks with two frozen open-weight agents, we build such curves for 47 and 60 failed trajectories and probe every step labeled by four frontier judges under the Traverse rubric. We find that the labels do not mark what a controller needs. Judges of different lineages agree on the exact step in only 21/57 cases, and the newest judges flag mistakes in 8/10 and 10/10 successful runs. For 66% of the labels, the agent's success probability does not drop at the labeled step; only 7/188 answers name the decisive step. Restarting at the measured restart point raises expected success from 0.44 to 0.57 offline, and real restarts confirm the advantage, whereas restarting at a judge's label does not (-0.08 to -0.03). We release our code, curves, and labels.

items.title: Explainable machine learning for anticipating county-level disaster recovery burden in the built environment
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop and evaluate an explainable machine-learning framework to anticipate county-level high recovery burden from natural disasters one year ahead using only public administrative and social-vulnerability data. Its substantive aim is to help built-environment decision makers shift from reactive post-event allocation to earlier, place-based prioritization of recovery and mitigation effort. Design/methodology/approach A county-year panel was assembled for 3,042 US counties over 2014–2022 by combining FEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries with county-level CDC/ATSDR social vulnerability index data. The outcome was a high-burden county-year, defined as repeated county-level declarations involving public assistance and/or hazard mitigation programme activity. Class-weighted logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost were benchmarked using a temporally ordered train-validation-test split. SHAP values and model coefficients were used to interpret predictive drivers. Findings The benchmark produced a moderate but decision-relevant predictive signal. Class-weighted logistic regression achieved the strongest out-of-sample performance on the hold-out period (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.626; area under the precision–recall curve 0.140; F1-score 0.262) and outperformed the more flexible tree-based models. Across models, stronger prior programme burden, recent major declarations, population size, mobile-home prevalence and social vulnerability were associated with higher next-year burden. Research limitations/implications The dependent variable is an administrative proxy for recovery burden rather than a direct measure of physical loss, repair cost or household recovery outcomes. The empirical setting is the USA; transfer to other countries should therefore be treated as conceptual and methodological rather than statistical. Practical implications The framework offers a transparent annual screening tool for local governments, regional planning bodies and emergency-management agencies seeking to identify counties likely to face elevated recovery pressure. Social implications Because it relies on public tabular data rather than expensive proprietary inputs, it is potentially transferable to resource-constrained settings that need interpretable anticipatory analytics. Originality/value The paper contributes a reproducible public-data pipeline that links explainable artificial intelligence to disaster-resilience planning in the built environment. It also responds to the journal’s growing interest in technology-enabled resilience by showing that interpretable models, rather than only complex algorithms, can support forward-looking preparedness and recovery prioritization.

items.title: Explanation User Interfaces: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is one of the major technological advancements of this century, bearing incredible potential for users through AI-powered applications and tools in numerous domains. Being often black-box (i.e., its decision-making process is unintelligible), developers typically resort to eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques to interpret the behavior of AI models to produce systems that are transparent, fair, reliable, and trustworthy. However, presenting explanations to the user is not trivial and is often left as a secondary aspect of the system’s design process, leading to AI systems that are not useful to end-users. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review on Explanation User Interfaces (XUIs) to gain a deeper understanding of the solutions and design guidelines employed in the academic literature to effectively present explanations to users. To improve the contribution and real-world impact of this survey, we also present a platform to support Human-cEnteRed developMent of Explainable user interfaceS (HERMES) and guide practitioners and scholars in the design and evaluation of XUIs.

items.title: Exploration on the Development of Adolescents' Sustained Physical Activity: PE Lessons, Teacher Support and School-Community Connection Modes
items.abstract: Teenagers lack sufficient exercise and are therefore not physically fit. According to the World Health Organization, children and adolescents aged 5-17 need to be physically active in a moderate-to-vigorous way for at least 60 minutes each day. However, a survey shows that 86% of children and teenagers are in a low-active state, and the compliance rate is only 14.8%. According to the "Compulsory Education Physical Education and Health Curriculum Standards (2022 Edition)", the average heart rate of students in physical education classes should be between 140 and 160 beats per minute. Insufficient teaching load and fragmented content are still relatively common in practice. The three contents of this paper are: the quality of physical education classes, teacher support and the connection between schools and communities; the way in which these three factors affect the continuous exercise of teenagers. The results show that the classroom serves as the foundation for skill acquisition, teacher autonomy support and emotional support motivate intrinsic motivation, and the link between schools and communities provides a space for extended participation outside of class. The three factors work together and are in conjunction to promote continuous participation behaviour. In light of the problems of skill-focused teaching in teacher support and a lack of school-community cooperation, it is proposed to optimise class load and teaching organisation, promote changes in the form of teacher support, and build a regular connection mechanism between schools and communities.

items.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration–exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders’ perceptions of environmental dynamism, employees’ AI use modes, leader temporal myopia, and employee radical creativity in the context of AI-enabled drug discovery. We distinguish leaders’ perceptions of environmental dynamism into perceived technological dynamism and perceived market dynamism, and employees’ AI use into exploratory and exploitative AI use. The model is tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling and three-wave matched survey data from 368 leader–employee dyads. The results show that leader-perceived technological dynamism is positively associated with employee exploratory AI use, whereas leader-perceived market dynamism is positively associated with employee exploitative AI use. Exploratory AI use is positively associated with employee radical creativity, whereas exploitative AI use is negatively associated with it. Leader temporal myopia weakens the positive conditional indirect relationship of technological dynamism with radical creativity through exploratory AI use and strengthens the negative conditional indirect relationship of market dynamism with radical creativity through exploitative AI use. By adopting a knowledge-activity perspective, this study reveals the differentiated relationships between AI use modes and radical creativity and further explains how perceptions of the external environment, leaders’ temporal orientation, and employees’ AI use behaviors are differentially related. The findings provide a theoretical basis and practical implications for helping firms engaged in AI-enabled drug discovery guide employees toward effective AI use and enhance radical creativity.

items.title: Explore with Memory, Learn without It: In-Context Exploration and Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Exploration bounds learning efficiency in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Current methods explore mostly through independent sampling, without fully using the information gathered along the way, such as known wrong answers and environment feedback. We propose LEAF, which injects a dynamic, problem-specific memory into the context before every rollout. The memory contains the most recent response, its reward, and other environment feedback. It is updated after every verifier call. We decouple policy updates from rollouts and update the policy through self-distillation. On four benchmarks and two open models, LEAF accelerates exploration by about 4x compared with a random sampling baseline. On unseen test sets, it improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by 1.59 and 1.83 percentage points on the two models, while using less compute than any RL baseline. These results highlight the potential of LEAF in improving both exploration and learning efficiency. Code is available at: https://github.com/on1262/LEAF

items.title: Exploring the Role of AI in Social Media Regulation: A Comparative Analysis of Selected South Asian Countries and the Actions of Major Technology Platforms
items.abstract: This article examines the extent to which private technology companies bear responsibility for respecting human rights, particularly freedom of expression, when governing social media content through artificial intelligence (AI), and how that responsibility relates to the legal obligations of States. It focuses on the rule-of-law complexities created by the interaction between territorially based public regulation and transnational platform governance. Through a comparative analysis of domestic law and platform practice, the article assesses how AI-mediated content moderation affects online expression. The revised analysis is limited to India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Afghanistan as selected comparative cases; it distinguishes State duties from the corporate responsibility to respect human rights, and treats AI-mediated moderation as including automated detection, classification, recommendation, down-ranking, removal and account restrictions. It proposes a seven-element human-rights test for AI-mediated moderation: legality, legitimate aim, necessity, proportionality, transparency, procedural fairness and effective remedy.

items.title: FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity
items.abstract: Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative to costly robot data collection for dexterous manipulation, but most human datasets lack force measurements. Dexterous manipulation requires not only visual and proprioceptive understanding but also the ability to anticipate and regulate interaction forces. To scale force-aware human-robot co-training, we introduce EgoForce, a large-scale human tactile dataset capturing force-rich manipulation experience, and combine it with robot demonstrations for pretraining. We present FACT, a robot foundation model that cascades from prospective visual planning to force-aware refinement for dexterous manipulation. FACT comprises two jointly trained components. A Track-Guided Coarse Planner jointly predicts actions, future video, and visual tracks. Future video and visual tracks also provide a shared task representation that facilitates cross-embodiment knowledge transfer and coarse action generation. Building on this coarse plan, a Force-Action Joint Refiner jointly predicts future force and refines the coarse action, allowing anticipated force and action to shape each other during refinement. We evaluate the model on ten tasks requiring fine-grained coordination and force feedback, including tool use, musical instruments, and precision laboratory procedures. Using as few as 10 robot trajectories with 90 human trajectories for fine-tuning, FACT outperforms both baselines, with success-rate gains of up to 60 percentage points over T-Rex. Ablations show that force supervision in human pretraining data is crucial for downstream robot performance after fine-tuning, while visual track prediction and training with future-force prediction improve dexterous execution. Experiments varying the human-robot data ratio during fine-tuning further suggest that FACT learns from human demonstrations nearly as effectively as from robot demonstrations.

items.title: Fair synthetic tabular data generation via disentangled semantic encoding and large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Synthetic tabular data generation plays a key role in alleviating data scarcity and privacy limitations in machine learning, especially in regulated domains such as finance and healthcare. While many existing methods focus on producing realistic and predictive tabular data, fairness is often not explicitly considered, leading to biased synthetic datasets. Recent approaches based on large language models (LLMs) further enhance data quality through natural language representations, which underscores the need for principled mechanisms that ensure fairness alongside predictive performance. To address this challenge, we propose SENNA, a framework that integrates disentangled semantic representations with LLM-based generation to jointly preserve utility and improve fairness. The framework separates task-relevant and task-independent information in the latent space and leverages these representations to guide generation and validation. Experimental results on three real-world datasets show that SENNA achieves competitive downstream performance, while substantially reducing both group-level disparities and individual-level inequality. We further evaluate the framework across multiple backbones, providing insights into fairness–utility trade-offs in LLM-based tabular data synthesis.

items.title: Fantastic Metrics and How to Find Them: Meta-Evaluating Metrics for Multi-lingual Style-Personalized Generation
items.abstract: Meta-evaluation of text generation metrics and LLM-judges is primarily conducted using metric-human correlations. However, prior work has shown that correlation is not an appropriate estimate of a metric's evaluation capability and can be unstable across evaluation settings, such as different datasets or languages. Therefore, we propose a regression-based meta-evaluation of metrics that learns on calibrated metric outputs to predict human ratings. We ground this measurement relative to a trivial constant-mean baseline and human agreements to provide a comparable measure of metric capability across evaluation settings. To test our meta-evaluation framework, we developed a large-scale multi-lingual style-personalized text generation (SPTG) benchmark, collecting multiple annotations across 10 topologically diverse languages and four evaluation dimensions, each with varying degrees of subjectivity. We meta-evaluated 32 metrics from three style evaluation paradigms (string-based, embedding-based, and LLM-judges) and their ensembles over these 40 evaluation settings. Our analysis revealed that even simple string- and embedding-based measurements can match strong LLM-judges when calibrated to human ratings. We also identified characteristics of human annotations that determine metric performance, as well as conditions under which a metric ensemble outperforms its individual constituents.

items.title: FastEEP: Fast Intra-Instance Elastic Scaling for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: Large-scale expert parallelism (EP) has become the standard deployment configuration for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models in production. Meanwhile, the highly dynamic nature of LLM workloads requires providers to continuously adjust serving capacity to match fluctuating demand. Scaling MoE serving cannot be efficiently achieved by simply adding or removing serving instances; instead, it often requires resizing the EP group within an existing instance, which we refer to as intra-instance scaling.Existing inference engines primarily rely on instance-level scaling, which destroys and reconstructs entire serving instances, incurring substantial scaling overhead. We present FastEEP (Fast Elastic Expert Parallel), a fast intra-instance scaling system for MoE serving based on the principle of Partial Reuse. FastEEP reuses existing runtime state across worker execution, GPU memory, and communication by separating reusable execution structures from the resources activated by the current EP configuration. This separation enables coordinated resource reclamation and reconfiguration while preserving costly-to-reconstruct state, allowing fast EP scaling without full instance teardown and reconstruction. Our evaluation shows that FastEEP achieves 4.5x--11.7x faster scaling than the existing vLLM-based approach across different models, enabling efficient, fine-grained scaling of MoE serving.

items.abstract: Federated Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) activity-recognition systems learn from decentralized wearable and smart-home records with potentially incorrect labels, non-IID client distributions, and unequal edge-device resources.Our objective is to improve downstream learning from these labels while limiting harmful corrections and respecting auditing, review, and communication budgets.FedCuraLM addresses this objective by converting sensor records into deterministic Semantic Evidence Cards, obtaining candidate-constrained small language model (SLM) assessments, and calibrating and combining them with task-model, prototype, and temporal evidence. Conflict-aware decisions retain observed labels, apply provisional soft corrections, request trusted review, or quarantine uncertain samples without overwriting annotations. Review-grounded reliability and communication-budgeted multi-prototype exchange support collaboration, while resource-aware scheduling assigns feasible SLM tiers across heterogeneous devices. Extensive evaluation on WISDM-W, WISDM-P, and CASAS using controlled symmetric, semantic-asymmetric, instance-dependent, and temporal-boundary corruption under varying client heterogeneity reveals that FedCuraLM significantly improves downstream performance over recent baselines and improves lower-tail client outcomes, audit precision, selective-correction safety, calibration, and communication efficiency. Edge-device measurements characterize latency, memory, and energy trade-offs. The findings position federated label curation as a semantic, statistical, communication, and systems problem.

items.title: FedGraph: Defending Federated Large Language Model Fine-Tuning Against Backdoor Attacks via Graph-Based Aggregation
items.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) allows multiple clients to collaboratively adapt models without sharing raw data, offering strong privacy benefits. However, this setting is highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which malicious clients manipulate their updates to induce targeted behaviors while maintaining normal performance on benign inputs. In this work, we make a key observation specific to federated LLM fine-tuning: malicious clients tend to exhibit strong consistency in their model updates, whereas benign clients produce more diverse and dispersed updates. This structural difference is not well captured by existing defense methods, which typically rely on direct anomaly detection in high-dimensional parameter space and therefore struggle in the presence of entangled LLM updates. Motivated by this observation, we propose FedGraph, a graph-based aggregation framework that explicitly models relationships among client updates. By representing clients as nodes in a dynamically constructed graph and extracting structural features that characterize their relative positions and interactions, FedGraph derives compact client representations that effectively separate malicious and benign behaviors. These representations are then used to identify and suppress malicious contributions during aggregation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedGraph significantly improves backdoor defense. It consistently reduces attack success rates to below 10% while achieving high detection accuracy (95.5% on average) and a low false positive rate (2.33%), substantially outperforming existing federated learning defenses.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Shifts Form Before Competence: Treatment-Correlated Style Drift Confounds Surface-Form Evaluation of Adapter Specialization
items.abstract: Stacking task adapters on a frozen domain adapter is a common approach for modular specialization of large language models, usually justified by knowledge injection; whether the surface-form graders standard in this setting can measure such specialization validly has remained unexamined. Two challenges follow: isolating the domain layer’s marginal contribution under identical task training, and determining whether measured differences reflect competence or output form. In this work, both are addressed with a matched-arm DoRA ablation on a frozen Qwen 3.5 9B hybrid: a 242 M-parameter domain expert is trained on a licensed 27.8 M-token corpus, and byte-identical task adapters are trained flat, stacked (DFE-stacking), and jointly across three tasks and five conditions, with the key extraction pair replicated at a second training seed; every grader is audited by per-item failure classification and a dual-rater blind human re-grade with consensus adjudication. The principal finding is that fine-tuning shifts output form before competence: stacking yields no seen-task benefit; an apparent generalization collapse on an unseen schema reduces to a single, highly seed-stable formatting coercion that the domain layer dampens and task-mixture training eliminates, and most automated keyword-grading failures prove to be correct paraphrases, leaving no genuine capability loss detected on any instrument. Because such style drift is induced by the training condition itself, surface-sensitive grader error becomes bias aligned with experimental arms rather than noise. Three additional experiments extend the findings: the coercion replicates on Llama 3.1 8B (60% vs. 19% untuned); a pre-registered 240-item formatting-perturbation battery across four further unseen schemas and eight conventions reveals fine-tuned conditions ranking lowest under strict grading yet highest under format-normalized grading; and a matched-compute wrong-domain control shows the domain layer’s coercion dampening to be generic substrate regularization, while value integrity under the induced drift tracked the substrate’s domain. The principal contribution lies in the identification and quantification of this confound: surface-form evaluation of adapter specialization is structurally confounded, and per-item audits of the type released herein are a necessary component of specialization studies.

items.title: FinGREAT: Evaluating LLMs on Financial Graph-guided Retrieval And Typing
items.abstract: Financial disclosures express the underlying relationships of double-entry accounting through unstructured text. While financial LLM benchmarks predominantly emphasize question answering and classification, schema-guided evidence discovery remains relatively under-explored. We investigate whether open-weight LLMs can extract and classify evidence corresponding to predefined double-entry accounting relationships underlying the text. Using a financial accounting graph comprising 11 nodes (accounts) and 11 edges (transaction types), we evaluate mid-sized models from 5 open-weight families across 1,300 SEC 10-K Item 7 filings spanning 26 years, comparing their extraction performance against three proprietary models. Results reveal substantial differences in extraction volume, edge distributions, and cross-model agreement. Building on this study, we introduce a human-annotated relation classification benchmark comprising 483 passages across three financial accounting categories, evaluating 34 open-weight and 10 proprietary models. The strongest open-weight and proprietary models achieve 84.1\% and 92.8\% accuracy, respectively, with considerable variation across accounting categories. Our findings highlight the importance of evaluating evidence discovery and relation understanding separately, while investigating locally deployable models for scalable, privacy-sensitive financial analysis.

items.title: Flexible paper-based self-sensing biomechanical ergonomics monitoring system for early warning of carpal tunnel syndrome risks
items.abstract: One of the most prevalent workplace-related musculoskeletal disorders is Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), which is caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist due to prolonged improper wrist posture. Continuous monitoring of wrist posture is essential to prevent serious complications, including the need for surgery. Current monitoring methods are often limited by high cost and poor portability because they rely on expensive electronics, rigid sensors, or vision-based systems. Wearable, flexible sensing technologies have emerged as an attractive solution for early detection and prevention of musculoskeletal disorders, as well as for continuous health monitoring. This work presents a low-cost, wearable, flexible, silver-conductive ink-patterned paper patch for continuous wrist posture monitoring and identification of ergonomic factors associated with CTS. Silver nanoparticles were synthesised by a chemical reduction method owing to their high electrical conductivity and superior oxidation resistance compared with copper, and the silver conductive ink was formulated using suitable binders. The conductive ink pattern printed on a flexible paper substrate undergoes mechanical deformation during wrist movement, resulting in detectable variations in resistance that correlate with changes in wrist bending angle. An Arduino-based system continuously monitored the resistance variations using a threshold-based algorithm, while an HC-05 Bluetooth module and a custom MIT App Inventor application wirelessly transmitted the wrist posture status to a smartphone. Experimental evaluation demonstrated accurate real-time detection of wrist posture with successful wireless ergonomic feedback. The proposed paper-based wearable system provides a lightweight, flexible, and cost-effective solution for the early detection and warning of potentially risky wrist position associated with CTS in industrial workers and computer users.

items.title: Fluorescent and Optical Sensors for Real-Time Detection of Waterborne Contaminants
items.abstract: Contamination of water by microbial pathogens and chemical pollutants is a serious threat to human health, ecosystems, and industries globally. Conventional water quality surveillance techniques, like lab-based tests, have problems like delays, high cost, and complicated sample preparation, which act as a hindrance to serving real-time information. Fluorescent and optical sensors are an encouraging way out of such constraints, as they can be used to detect waterborne contaminants in real time and in situ. These are sensitive sensors, which can detect even low traces of contaminants and can provide quick data, which is vital in making prompt intervention during water treatment and in protecting human health. Fluorescent sensors are designed to monitor the fluorescent characteristics of the contaminants, whereas optical sensors are designed to monitor the interactions of light, including absorption, scattering, or reflection. They are especially applicable in on-site monitoring in a wide variety of conditions, such as remote or emergency situations, due to their portability and cost-effectiveness. Although they have their advantages, there are challenges that include interference by other substances, sensitivity to environmental factors, and degradation of the sensor. Yet, the combination of the development of nanomaterials, artificial intelligence, and wireless technology has excessive opportunities to improve the performance and increase the scope of these sensors. This chapter discusses the concepts, uses, benefits, and drawbacks of fluorescent and optical sensors and the future of their use in transforming the world in its water-quality monitoring.

items.title: Fostering team learning for educational innovation: An academic development initiative on genAI and assessment
items.abstract: Abstract Drawing on the notion of workplace learning this study examines how academic development can design and facilitate team learning in the academic workplace to support co-constructive educational innovation. Based on a qualitative case study at a Swiss University of Teacher Education, it analyses a participatory initiative addressing generative artificial intelligence (genAI) in assessment. The staged process combined SWOT-based collective sense-making, a design sprint, selective project funding, and facilitated reflection during project development. Data consisted of process documentation and collaboratively generated written reflections, which were analysed and refined through iterative feedback and co-writing. The findings show how structured formats, shared artefacts, and deliberate facilitation enabled participants to make distributed expertise visible, develop shared problem understandings, form project teams, and move from exchange towards co-construction and coordinated experimentation. At the same time, public pitching, funding decisions, time pressures, and institutional constraints created tensions between collaboration and competition, openness and focus, and participation and decision-making. The study suggests that academic development can support educational innovation by acting as facilitator, trust-building broker, and co-learner. Its contribution lies in conceptualising participatory innovation processes as workplace-learning arrangements that connect emerging team-learning processes with local experimentation and wider institutional conversations, while recognising that organisational learning requires further institutional uptake.

items.title: Foundation Models for Event Prediction Across Heterogeneous Event Logs
items.abstract: Event logs are ubiquitous across real-world domains, including business processes, manufacturing workflows, healthcare, and many other operational systems. Yet event logs can differ substantially in their event semantics, label spaces, interaction patterns, and temporal scales, making it difficult to build a single foundation model that generalizes directly to previously unseen systems. We address this challenge with the Foundation Event Predictor (FEP), a simple and scalable in-context architecture that performs next-event prediction through learned, event-level nonparametric inference. Causal self-attention encodes context and target histories into key and query representations, respectively, while the observed next context events are encoded as values. Cross-attention then performs learned, relevance-weighted aggregation of next-event outcomes over all context transitions, allowing the entire nonparametric prediction procedure to be expressed as standard attention operations and efficiently parallelized with modern kernels such as FlashAttention. To promote cross-system generalization, we introduce permutation-robust embedding learning and random fixed embeddings to decouple event IDs from persistent semantics, together with empirical quantile transforms and robust normalization to handle diverse temporal scales. We pretrain FEP on 696 real-world event datasets spanning heterogeneous event systems and evaluate it on 50 held-out datasets unseen during pretraining. Across these datasets, FEP generalizes effectively to new event systems without parameter adaptation, frequently approaching the performance of strong models trained separately on each target dataset while substantially outperforming existing foundation-model baselines, particularly on challenging prediction tasks.

items.title: Fractal Information Dynamics – Part 2
items.abstract: We propose Fractal Information AI (FIAI), a graph-based architecture for adaptive learning in which knowledge is represented as recursively organized information structures and learning actions are prioritized by validated information gain, uncertainty reduction, network propagation, and decision relevance. The framework originates from a fractal-tree interpretation in which branches carry information, knots encode rule families, and paths represent inferential relations. For artificial intelligence, the logical notion of formal provability is retained only where machine-checkable verification is available; in open-domain settings it is generalized to an evidence-validation or consistency gate. Each knowledge node carries an unresolved-state variable, provenance, verifier status, information-gain estimate, decision relevance, and propagation weights. A Learning Efficiency Metric (LEM) quantifies validated uncertainty reduction per available unresolved mass or, in cost-aware form, per unit acquisition/computation cost. Multiple agents exchange validated knowledge through bound coupling operators, allowing the study of knowledge hubs, bottlenecks, redundancy, and emergent collaborative structures. We derive deterministic and stochastic node dynamics, stability conditions for propagation, and bounds on cross-agent transfer. A reproducible numerical illustration with three interacting 20-node knowledge trees demonstrates LEM trajectories, decreasing unresolved mass, and node-level utility concentration. FIAI is presented as a testable architectural hypothesis rather than a demonstrated replacement for transformer, graph-neural, retrieval-augmented, or multi-agent systems. Its central empirical claim is that explicit knowledge-utility accounting can improve the allocation of learning and verification resources under fixed budgets.

items.title: Fractal-Inspired Biorefineries for Sustainable Polymer Production: A Conceptual Framework Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Industry 5.0
items.abstract: The transition from petroleum-derived polymers to renewable materials requires biorefineries capable of managing the compositional variability and multiscale structure of lignocellulosic biomass. This conceptual narrative review examines fractal-inspired principles—including hierarchical organization, branching, modularity, and finite-range statistical self-similarity—as a design perspective for integrated biorefineries. Deterministic mathematical fractals are distinguished from statistical fractals and hierarchical engineered systems, and methods for characterizing scale-dependent surfaces, porous catalysts, and transport networks are reviewed. The coordinated valorization of cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin is then considered within an integrated biomass-to-chemicals framework for producing platform chemicals, functional materials, and polymer precursors. Petroleum crude-to-chemicals processing, including the S-OIL Shaheen Project, is discussed as a limited industrial benchmark for integrated fractionation, residue upgrading, and product diversification rather than as direct evidence of fractal engineering. An integrated framework is proposed in which fractal-inspired design provides the physical and organizational architecture, artificial intelligence supports characterization, prediction, optimization, and control, and Industry 5.0 provides the objectives of sustainability, resilience, and human-centered manufacturing. The framework remains conceptual. Its potential benefits must be evaluated through transport modeling, mass and energy balances, process simulation, experimental comparison, techno-economic analysis, and life-cycle assessment.

items.title: FRACTION: Fraud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context Navigation
items.abstract: Graph fraud explanation generation emerges as an important task, which requires jointly leveraging graph structure and content information to produce human-readable explanations for a given risk label. An intuitive approach is to adapt existing graph-enhanced large language models (LLMs), which inject graph structure into LLMs via graph-conditioned instruction tuning or structure-aware embeddings. However, existing methods face two key challenges in graph fraud explanation generation: a lack of evaluation protocols tailored to explanation quality, and a mismatch between the granularity of graph information they provide and what explanation generation requires. In this paper, we propose FRaud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context NavigaTION (FRACTION), a framework for graph fraud explanation generation. To evaluate explanation quality, we introduce a task-specific rubric that assesses faithfulness, graph grounding, helpfulness, consistency, and conciseness, and validate it against human judgments. To focus on fine-grained details of relevant neighbors without reading the entire neighborhood, we equip a language model with graph tools that progressively disclose neighbor records. To train our graph agent, we propose a rubric-guided trajectory distillation strategy through which the agent learns both tool-use behavior and structured explanation generation. Experimental results on three fraud datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under a human-aligned rubric.

items.title: From Behavioral Theory to Chairside Decision Support: Development of ELIGE AI, a Hybrid Rule-Based and Large Language Model Tool for the Behavioral Management of Dental Caries
items.abstract: Background: Dental caries is the most prevalent noncommunicable disease worldwide. Within the DCIEH framework it is a dysbiosis of the dental biofilm microbiome that is regulated by biology, modulated by behavior and conditioned by the environment. It is also a trans-complex disease whose outcome emerges from the interaction of biological, behavioral and socio-environmental factors. Behavioral sciences offer mature theories to explain and change oral health behaviors, but a persistent gap separates these theories from routine chairside care. In 2024 we proposed ELIGE/CHOOSE, a theoretical framework that integrates Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) and the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model into three clinical phases: Identify, Articulate and Plan.Objective: To report the systematic development of ELIGE AI, a clinical decision support tool that operationalizes the ELIGE/CHOOSE framework through an evidence-based, author-designed deterministic algorithm combined with a large language model (LLM).Methods: Development was guided by the Medical Research Council framework for complex interventions, the ORBIT model and the IDEAS framework for digital behavior change interventions. Reporting draws on TIDieR, DECIDE-AI and TRIPOD-LLM. Development proceeded in five phases: (1) theoretical integration of SCT, COM-B, the Transtheoretical Model, the Health Action Process Approach, motivational interviewing and Intervention Mapping; (2) translation into a stepwise clinical protocol; (3) formalization of the first author's clinical reasoning as an explicit decision algorithm, with every rule traceable to theory or evidence; (4) integration of an LLM restricted to bounded language tasks; and (5) iterative build-and-refine cycles across versions informed by clinical use.Results: ELIGE AI (v3.9) is a web application with seven screens across the three ELIGE/CHOOSE phases plus a follow-up module. In about 20 to 25 minutes it produces a specified behavior, a principal COM-B determinant with a displayed rationale, a graded goal ladder, Behaviour Change Technique Taxonomy v1 techniques matched to the determinant, rule-based referrals and personalized patient materials. At follow-up it re-measures the same constructs, behavior frequency and dental caries risk, and recommends the next step on the same behavioral route. The algorithm makes every clinical decision; the LLM only drafts and classifies; the clinician validates and can override every output.Conclusions: ELIGE AI shows how a published behavioral framework and its author's clinical reasoning can be encoded as a transparent algorithm and safely combined with generative AI. The tool now enters a three-stage evaluation of usability, feasibility and validity, and efficacy on dental caries outcomes.

items.title: From Circuits to Policies: A Review and Taxonomy of Decision Making and Strategy Selection in LLMs and LLM Agents
items.abstract: Large language models and the agents built on them can reach the same outcome through different internal computations, reasoning trajectories, and system-level policies. Existing reviews typically treat mechanistic interpretability, reasoning, agent architectures, and safety separately, leaving no common framework for analyzing how a system represents alternatives, evaluates them, commits to one, executes it, and revises that choice. This article presents a structured review and a faceted taxonomy of decision making and strategy selection in LLMs and LLM-based agents. The framework separates system locus—model, harness, or their tested interaction—from temporal scope—a single forward pass or call, a reasoning episode, or an agent trajectory—and decomposes decision making into six functional stages from state representation to update or termination. Five claim-specific evidential relations distinguish behavioral observation, representation decoding, causal influence, controlled manipulation, and mechanistic explanation, while robustness is assessed separately across prompts, tasks, models, harness configurations, and independent replication. Across the literature, evidence is strongest for local mechanisms within individual model calls and substantially weaker for persistent strategies across agent trajectories. The central unresolved gap is cross-scope continuity: few studies follow the same decision variable from internal representation through commitment, executed action, and subsequent feedback. A July 2026 agent-security incident is used to illustrate how the framework converts observed coordination and constraint circumvention into testable causal hypotheses.

items.title: From digital skilling to sustainable performance: How climate entrepreneurship and attitudes toward artificial intelligence shape the future of SME technological transitions
items.abstract: Digital technologies are reshaping how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies respond to environmental pressure, yet two questions remain open. Research linking digital skilling to sustainability has largely tested direct effects without tracing the behavioral pathway such an effect would have to travel, and attitudes toward artificial intelligence have rarely been examined as a condition governing whether green entrepreneurial activity converts into performance. This study addresses both. Integrating the Theory of Planned Behavior, Diffusion of Innovations Theory, and Contingency Theory into a single explanatory sequence, it models climate entrepreneurship (CE), green entrepreneurial behavior (GEB), and green entrepreneurial intention (GEI) as the mechanisms linking digital entrepreneurial education and training (DEET) to sustainable environmental performance (SEP) and sustainable organizational performance (SOP), with commitment to the environment (CTE) and attitude toward artificial intelligence (ATAI) as boundary conditions. Survey data from 648 Pakistani SMEs are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, with a random forest robustness check confirming that the modelled relationships are linear and compensatory. DEET directly predicts organizational performance but has no significant direct effect on environmental performance; its environmental influence is transmitted entirely through the three behavioral mechanisms. Environmental commitment and favorable attitudes toward artificial intelligence each strengthen the conversion of green entrepreneurship into sustainability outcomes, though the interaction effects are modest in magnitude. The findings suggest that digital skilling initiatives are unlikely to yield environmental returns unless paired with entrepreneurial agency and technological openness, with implications for the sequencing of digital and AI-readiness policy in resource-constrained economies.

items.title: From Instrument to Co-Creator: Authorship in Generative and AI Music
items.abstract: This paper presents the evolving concept of authorship in music creation as algorithmic and artificial intelligence systems impact the musical market. Based on Philip Galanter's definition of generative art, the paper discusses about the authorship of music in different senerios: when it is generated by tools like Nyquist or AI models such as Suno. The argument is structured around three distinct ways of human-machine interaction: human-led creation where computers are used as instruments; human-guided creation, where algorithms are restricted to a predetermined range of randomness; and human-crafted prompts, where AI generates the music completely. Following the analysis of these cases and some complex instances, this paper concludes that authorship is decided by the location of creativity and intentionality rather than a fixed attribute. The analysis reveals that authorship belongs to different subjects accordingly to different methods humans used to use generative tools: following the primary source of meaning contribution. Ultimately, the paper argues that the central issue may not be the authorship itself, but the human need for music to serve as a bridge for shared meaning and emotional connection.
